{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABbVds8Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhE6RUI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 120, "title": "Default the browser demo to PC-9821Ap DOS and automatically route inserted media, with manual drive overrides", "body": "## Problem

The public browser demo currently starts with **PC-9801VM** selected and **floppy drive 1** selected in its `Drive` dropdown. That is an unnecessarily narrow and error-prone starting point for a demo whose **PC-9821Ap DOS** profile supports more PC-98 DOS hardware, including **IDE HDI** boot, Japanese CG, 16/256-color video and additional CPU/device features. The two bundled MIT demos still use floppy media.

The `Drive` dropdown currently mixes two different ideas: **where to insert a file** and **which medium boots**. The user must know to choose IDE before supplying a `.hdi`, otherwise the default floppy size check produces `Floppy image exceeds 4 MiB.`; choosing the wrong media slot can also cause avoidable extension errors. In `web/app.js`, the file chooser and drag-and-drop both use `$('drive').value`, insertion into drive 0/2 triggers reset and boot, and drive 1 is a non-booting insertion. The underlying `Machine::insert` selects the HDD boot source for IDE, and floppy boot for drive 0.

We want an intuitive default that works for DOS games without removing control from users who need a specific historical profile or multiple floppy drives. Follow the repository's [UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/README.md#uiux): keep it simple; show, don't tell; intuitive and predictable.

## Expected outcome

1. **New-page default machine: `PC-9821Ap DOS`**. It is the browser demo's initial selected profile, including the actual Wasm Rust guest core/profile, title/profile badge, and appropriate display information. Keep **`PC-9801VM` selectable** and working for software requiring it. This changes the **browser demo's initial selection**; avoid changing the Rust library/headless default profile unless independently necessary, since those callers and fixtures have their own explicit contracts.
2. **New-page default drive: `Auto`**. The file extension selects where compatible media is inserted:
   - `.hdi` (case insensitive) → **IDE HDD (drive 2)**, valid on **PC-9821Ap DOS** only, and boot automatically.
   - Supported floppy images `.tfd`, `.hdm`, `.xdf`, `.2hd`, `.d88`, `.d98`, `.img` (case insensitive) → **floppy 1 (drive 0)** and boot automatically.
   - The above applies consistently to the **file picker and drag-and-drop**; validate the real format/header/size using the existing Rust parser, not just an extension. Do not try to mount a `.hdi` as a floppy and report the misleading 4 MiB floppy error.
3. **Manual overrides remain available:** select **Floppy 1**, **Floppy 2**, or **IDE HDD** explicitly. These choices must control the insertion destination (including floppy 2's **no automatic reboot** behavior) and must not be silently replaced by automatic routing. If the user selects PC-9801VM and an HDI, give an actionable message that IDE requires PC-9821Ap, **without silently switching machine profiles**; manual media-drive mismatches should fail clearly rather than silently reroute.
4. **Boot/reset behavior stays predictable:** inserting into automatically chosen floppy 1 or IDE boots that guest as intended; reset retains mounted media and the selected boot source, including when multiple media are mounted; explicit floppy 2 insertion must not change the boot source or restart the guest. The UI should not introduce a second independent boot-priority selector unless proven necessary. If both bootable media are mounted, the current active boot source must be visible/understandable and deterministically preserved on reset; do not let a stale Auto selector silently choose a different medium.
5. **Mounted-media actions are unambiguous in Auto mode:** after an automatic insertion, clearly show the **resolved target drive and media filename**; ensure **Eject** and **Export disk** apply to the intended actual drive rather than an invalid `Auto` sentinel. On manual selection, show/operate on that selected drive, including drive 2 and drive 1. Handle no-media states and a profile change consistently.
6. Both bundled **Star Trail** and **Hello world + BEEP** must still boot and work at the new PC-9821Ap default, remain usable when PC-9801VM is selected, and must mount/boot from floppy 1 even if the user previously chose IDE or floppy 2. Do not hardcode fake guest results or add third-party game assets.

## Context and reproduction

Relevant current code:

- [`web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/index.html) renders `<select id="profile">` with PC-9801VM first and `<select id="drive">` with floppy `1 · boot` selected first.
- [`web/app.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/app.js) uses `insert`, `loadBytes`, `loadFile`, drag/drop, `showMedia`, `exportBytes`, `bundled`, reset and profile-change handlers.
- [`src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/lib.rs) `Machine::insert` sets the boot source according to insertion into IDE or FDD1; drive 2 requires Ap.
- [`README.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/README.md) documents current default and manual boot behavior; its browser help/footnote has some old profile-limit wording. Update relevant user-facing documentation in scope.

Current reproduction: with a fresh page, try loading a local `aliceY3.hdi` **without touching the `Drive` selector**. The browser sends it to drive 0 and may emit a *floppy* size error. For mandatory tests use **original MIT HDI/floppy probes or licensed FreeDOS controls**, never this private adult/game media.

### Scope and compatibility principles

- **UI default and media-routing change, not a general emulator hardware upgrade.** Preserve the capability limits and error reporting of each profile. No changes to emulator CPU/device behavior just to make more titles appear supported.
- Keep simple accessible labels/semantics and responsive layout; minimize redundant selectors or explanatory paragraphs.
- Respect explicit user selections; no surprise profile changes.
- Do not add private HDIs, copyrighted games, adult media, BIOS/font ROM dumps, or other restricted assets to the repository, CI, browser web assets or screenshots.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fresh browser session selects **PC-9821Ap DOS** in the DOM and in the running Rust/Wasm guest profile, and selects **Auto** for media destination. Its initial profile label/display information and keyboard/mouse state are consistent with the actual machine.
- [ ] With **Auto** selected, a valid original/licensed `.hdi` goes to IDE drive 2 and boots; each supported floppy type routes to FDD1 and boots. Check both file picker and drag/drop paths, case-insensitive names, and supported size/format validation. Reject malformed/oversized/unsupported media through the correct helpful error path.
- [ ] With **manual drive selection**, FDD1, FDD2 and IDE receive the requested images and their semantics do not change; FDD2 insertion does **not** reset/change active boot; manual mismatches are explained rather than silently rerouted. With **PC-9801VM manually selected**, HDI insertion is rejected with a clear message without silently changing the selected profile.
- [ ] **Reset, eject and export work in Auto and manual modes** and remain mapped to the intended actual drive; show mounted filename, actual drive and active boot source clearly enough that users can tell what will reboot. Verify multiple mounted disks and profile switching do not unexpectedly corrupt/delete media or boot the wrong source.
- [ ] **Star Trail** and **Hello world + BEEP** still boot through their real guest code from FDD1 on **both profiles**, including from the new initial Ap state and after a previous manual IDE/FDD2 selection; no host-scripted output. Retain keyboard/audio/save behavior already covered by browser tests.
- [ ] Add/update **real production-Wasm Chromium browser tests** for the initial machine and Auto routing, both upload paths, manual overrides, both built-in demos, reset/eject/export and error states. Run those tests at **both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`**, cold and after applicable reset. Reuse **rights-cleared existing guest fixtures** rather than fetching or publishing a proprietary HDI.
- [ ] Update README/demo help/footnote to describe the new Ap default, automatic drive routing, manual override, correct per-profile compatibility limits and reset semantics. Avoid obsolete text suggesting the core still lacks features that are already supported; do not rewrite unrelated hardware docs.
- [ ] Run the repository's applicable fixture/license preparation, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, production Rust/Wasm build and exact public-assets audit, and complete Chromium acceptance on both roots. Report actual results and failures; **the current `main` Emulator acceptance run [#41146277227](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/actions/runs/41146277227) failed in `npm test` despite prior PR checks passing**, so distinguish any baseline CI/browser failure from a regression caused by this Issue. If an unrelated infrastructure/test failure persists, record it and create a separate English `task` Issue instead of disguising it as success.
- [ ] PR title/body and commits in English; review against this Issue; do not require a deployed GitHub Pages check, manual gameplay or external media before merge.

## Optional validation

Manual browser usability check on a local build for first-time users on desktop/mobile: drag a known-good floppy, choose IDE for a legal HDI, insert a second floppy, switch machine profiles, and inspect Auto/media-action clarity. Not a pre-merge gate.

## Required post-merge verification

None. GitHub Pages deployment or a separate runtime-operations failure can be tracked in its own `task` Issue if needed.
